chunks: Yunus from Al-A'ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The servant will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment with blood moistening him, so something resembling a cupping cup or more than that would be handed over to him, and it would be said to him, 'This is your share from the blood of so-and-so.' So he would say, 'O Lord, You know that You caused me to die and I had not spilled any blood.' So He would say, 'Yes, you heard a report of such and such from so-and-so, and you reported it upon him, and it was transmitted until it came to so-and-so the tyrant, and he was killed because of it, and this is your share from his blood.'

key_terms.الْمِحْجَمَةِ: The cupping cup (a measure of blood)

ai.seo_question: How does transmitting knowledge lead to bearing the blood of the killed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the mechanism of 'sharing in the blood' (sahm min damihi) by tracing the chain of transmission from a scholar to a ruler, highlighting how the mere act of publicizing knowledge can lead to martyrdom. It underscores the spiritual accountability of the narrator, distinguishing between direct killing and the indirect consequence of one's report reaching a tyrant, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence of knowledge transmission.

en.hubeali: Yunus, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The servant will be Resurrected on the Day of Judgment moistened in blood, so there would be handed over to him something resembling the cupping or more than that, and it would be said to him, ‘This is your share from the blood of so and so’. So he would be saying, ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> Know that you<sup>azwj</sup> Caused me to die and I had not spilt any blood!’ So He<sup>azwj</sup> would be Saying: “Yes. You heard a report from so and so of such and such, for you reported upon it, and it got transmitted until it came to be to so and so tyrant, and he was killed upon it, and this is your share from his blood’.
en.sarwar: 5. Yunus has narrated from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “

I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘A servant (of Allah) will be raised on the Day of Judgment, although he had not caused any bloodshed, something containing a dose or more blood will be given to him and he will be told, “This is your share of the blood of so and so.” He will say, ‘Lord, You know that You caused me to die and I had not committed any bloodshed.’ The Lord will say, ‘Yes, you did commit bloodshed. You heard such and such facts from so and so, you narrated it against his interests and transmitted it until it reached so and so tyrant, who murdered him on the basis of the narration, and this is your share of that blood.’”
